nodes.label: docs/canon/DESIGN_HISTORY.md — how this system was actually designed and built, 2026-05-07 → 2026-08-03: one timeline fused from two independent forensic records plus the verbatim user canon, in six eras, followed by the eighteen contradictions adjudicated in numeric order. Interpretation, produced 2026-08-03, unreviewed: nothing here is new research and nothing here is a new conclusion — every statement already exists in a source record and arrives with the citation that record carries, while the selection and ordering of what appears is agent judgement.

The three sources, and what each can settle. docs/canon/raw/git_record.md covers 2026-05-07 → 08-01 in 74 commits, 30 refs and 91 git show reproduce commands, and settles what existed when, what changed, what was deleted and whether a later state contradicts an earlier one — never who wrote prose. docs/canon/raw/desktop_docs_record.md covers 2026-05-25 → 07-12 in 20 desktop-only agent-written handoff/state docs, 6,719 lines, ~150 recovered user quotes, and settles the decision conversations git cannot see — second-hand, an agent's report of a conversation. docs/canon/USER_CANON.md carries 803 verbatim human turns 05-14 → 08-03 plus 80 recovered rulings and settles what the user actually said. The corpus has grown since this file was written and the figures are dated, not wrong: 803 turns to 08-03 is exactly what raw/user_turns_all.jsonl held at b0fcadc, the snapshot this file was read against, while at HEAD the corpus is 1,304 turns, 2026-05-14 → 2026-08-13T18:10:01Z, and USER_CANON.md is 1,589 lines rather than 1,577 — nothing below was re-read against the added turns.

Citation rule and authorship labels. Every statement keeps the evidence its source record carried: a git claim carries its git show <ref>:<path> command exactly as git_record.md gives it; a docs claim carries the desktop doc's filename and heading; a user quote carries date plus the quote, and where USER_CANON.md holds it that is said so the two files stay linked. A claim without its citation is a defect. Authorship labels are kept from both records and never silently upgraded: from git_record.md, [USER] (first-person design voice, terse human commit register), [AGENT] (AI footer, or the mechanical feat: update <dir> (N files) tooling format) and [UNKNOWN] (undecidable from git — most May/June prose); from desktop_docs_record.md, [USER-STATED] (verbatim quote or attributed ruling), [USER-STATED — paraphrase] (attributed ruling, agent's wording), [AGENT-ASSERTED] (proposal, synthesis, or agent-run measurement) and [UNCLEAR].

Precedence when the two records disagree about who decided something: first-hand chat > git blob > agent-written doc. A [CHAT] turn in USER_CANON.md outranks everything; a git blob proves a thing existed but can never attribute prose; an agent-written state doc is the only attribution evidence for the two chat blackouts and is used as such, labelled second-hand. Where the records genuinely disagree, both readings appear and the better-evidenced one is named, with the unsettled ones collected at the end.

The blackouts are not the only gap: the extractor filters the whole record, end to end. tools/canon_extract.py:118-121 rejects any user record carrying a toolUseResult key or a tool_result content block before considering its text, so a [CHAT] absence is never by itself proof he said nothing, at any date. How much that costs is known for one half and not the other: the desktop half's report enumerates the bucket in full — 620 tool_result rejects yielding zero characters of human text (min 0, max 0) and 0 records across all 71 files carrying both a text and a tool_result block, provably empty of human prose, so the eras this file covers most heavily are not weakened by the filter; the laptop half (793 turns, from 2026-07-06) reports 2,530 tool_result rejects and never enumerates them, with its exhaustive false-negative check scoped to the text-matching rule. So a [CHAT] gap before 07-06 is a real gap in the conversation; a gap after it may be an artefact of extraction.

The era map, 2026-05-07 → 2026-08-03, one timeline fused from two independent forensic records. Era 1, 05-07 → 05-24: frames and facets — the system arrives fully designed, and starts shedding parts. Era 2, 05-25 → 06-14: the v2 rebuild pivot — references not copies, and the weights stop being emitted. Era 3, 06-15 → 06-28: facet reconciliation and the v3 harness — the spec that was never built. Era 4, 06-28 → 07-12: the native artefact build, and its condemnation by its own author. Era 5, 07-13 → 07-28: the v1 retrieval engineering era — the forensic arm becomes the product. Era 6, 07-29 → 08-03: audit, corpus, tag-first — and the canon audit that produced these records. 06-28 is a hinge day and appears in two eras: the commits that close era 3 and the 123-turn build session that opens era 4 happen on the same date.

Era 1 — frames and facets, 2026-05-07 → 2026-05-24. Evidence asymmetry stated up front: the design arrives complete in the first commit. What was decided: the system arrives fully designed (05-07); the original graph spine (05-07); the controlled canonical vocabulary (05-07); the cluster-dimension rename (05-11, [USER] — theme→topic, object_entity→entities, event_process→activity, time_relevance→temporal, information_need→evidence); interpretation frames, the model must not see pipeline machinery (05-13); the tagging contract and its five-facet scoring schema (05-14); the query interpretation layer with prompt/chunk symmetry (05-14); and the full-HERB pilot, the empirical basis (05-14). What diverged: the canonical vocabulary was deleted with no mention (C-3); two extra scoring factors arrive between design and ship, 05-18 → 05-28 (C-12); the jockedev2 RAGAS series is written and then squashed away (C-11); and two undefended constants go into 255,288 edges (C-15).

Era 2 — the v2 rebuild pivot, 2026-05-25 → 2026-06-14. 05-25: the weight/retrieval redesign, then the live audit that shelved it — the empirical basis for everything after. 05-30: the v2 pivot, references not copies. 06-01: the three-tier semantic model. 06-03/06-04: chunking and the cap. 06-09: weights — measure, don't emit. 06-11: the re-cut — phrase nodes, no description, the build gate. 06-12: the spine closes — file → chunk → tags, nothing else is a node, records-as-nodes dead, no value inventories in the graph, chunk→file value killed. 06-14: facets as relevance channels, and the thesis is done. What diverged: the shipped v1 scorer with seven factors and five hard gates (05-28); D10 is never retracted in place (C-1); the SQL-agent baseline is adopted, then silently un-adopted; and the five-facet set enters as an agent synthesis and is treated as canon.

Era 3 — facet reconciliation and the v3 harness, 2026-06-15 → 2026-06-28. 06-15 is the largest design landing in the repo: the closed graph spine lands, the chunking design as coherent episodes, the mapping key, structural oracle quarantine, the v2 facet set and per-facet specs — the spec that was never built — the retrieval routing model, and model contracts as a working draft with nine unsigned items. 06-18 → 06-23: the three-arm eval harness, arm independence and comment hygiene. 06-21: the lucene baseline. 06-25: three documents in one day. 06-27: the chat record resumes. What was built: the built tagger, facets abandoned (06-28), and the fourth facet set, the content profile (06-27). What diverged: the per-facet extraction spec was fully written and never built (C-7); DESIGN.md contradicts itself at the same commit (C-9); three tagger-model decisions, the third undocumented (C-10); the leaderboard-comparable anchor metric was specced, stubbed, then deleted (C-17); and design-bearing changes hidden under tooling commit messages (C-18).

Era 4 — the native artefact build and its condemnation, 2026-06-28 → 2026-07-12. The 06-28 123-turn session reconstructed turn-by-turn; what pass 1 actually is, from the code record; the pass-1 result [AGENT-ASSERTED], gold-100, k=10, retrieval-only. 06-30 / 07-01: pass 2 — dials, the curve, and the relationships pivot. 07-06: the v1 arm is revived, renamed and restated. 07-12: the state of things, and the artefact_v1 audit. What diverged: C-7 is resolved here, in a four-step bridge from spec to flat list; C-2's causal chain completes and the contradiction does not yet exist; the canon goes stale on 06-28 and the staleness is logged the same day (C-14); and a list of what was specified in this era and never built.

Era 5 — the v1 retrieval engineering era, 2026-07-13 → 2026-07-28, in which the forensic arm becomes the product. 07-15: the four-point rejection of the gate. 07-16: trust revoked, and the terminal becomes canon. 07-17 → 07-24: the usage catastrophes. 07-20 → 07-21: the vocabulary is reclaimed. 07-22: orchestrator mode and the adversarial panel. 07-23: normalization, the hybrid arm, and commit-means-push. 07-25 → 07-26: what the score is for, and which artefact is which. 07-28: the graph question again, and the full revert. What was built: the shipped artefact arm. What diverged: three canon rules and the arm that ships now disagree at HEAD, plus what git cannot supply for this era.

Era 6 — audit, corpus, tag-first, 2026-07-29 → 2026-08-03. 07-29: held-out generalization, on his terms. 07-30: what tags are for. 07-31: the fullest clustering specification, and a reversal. 08-01: tags-first ships, and is immediately rejected. 08-02: gold-blindness, and the canon audit. 08-03: the two machines' history is merged. What diverged: the full revert took the matched-budget work with it; cluster-K has never been on the load-bearing path; the arbitrary constants he predicted, unenumerated; and the graph question, asked seven times, never answered.

The eighteen contradictions, adjudicated. C-numbers are fixed at discovery in git_record.md and are never renumbered, because other documents cite them; git_record.md's by-importance order is preserved at the head of the section while the adjudications run in numeric order so existing references resolve. The three statuses used are genuine silent drop, documented reversal, and user decision misread as drift — plus not a contradiction where both records verified an item as sound, and split where the two halves of one C-number resolve differently.

C-1 through C-5. C-1 — D10 reversed, content-in-graph → references-only. C-2 — the v2 design declared all v1 eval numbers invalid, and the shipped arm is the v1 graph. C-3 — the controlled canonical vocabulary was deleted with no mention. C-4 — six of eight node labels and four of seven edge types disappeared. C-5 — "the chunk description is dead", except in the arm that ships.

C-6 through C-12. C-6 — the condemned v1 facets returned under new names. C-7 — the per-facet extraction spec was fully written and never built. C-8 — entity decomposition specified, then reversed. C-9 — DESIGN.md contradicts itself in two places at the same commit. C-10 — three tagger-model decisions, each superseding the last, the final one undocumented. C-11 — six commits of measured results were squashed away. C-12 — "seven factors": the claim is correct.

C-13 through C-18. C-13 — "the model emits no numbers, ever" against the arm that ships. C-14 — canon describes a build state that no longer exists. C-15 — two constants that no artifact in git ever derives. C-16 — "No hard filters anywhere in ranking", written against a v1 that was full of them. C-17 — the leaderboard-comparable anchor metric was specced, stubbed, then deleted. C-18 — design-bearing changes routinely hidden under tooling commit messages.

The resolved-status table and its tally. Genuine silent drop: 3 — C-3 (an entire subsystem removed with one table cell, no user statement in any source), C-11 (of the commit record, not the knowledge), C-14 (of the fix: canon went stale 2026-06-28, the staleness was logged the same day, the repair was never applied). Documented reversal: 6 — C-1, C-6, C-7, C-8, C-16, C-17. User decision misread as drift: 3 — C-2, C-5, C-13. Not a contradiction, verified: 3 — C-12, C-15, C-18. Split across two statuses: 3 — C-4, C-9, C-10. Total 18. Live at HEAD: C-2, C-5, C-9, C-10, C-13, C-14, C-15, C-16, C-17, C-18 — where HEAD means 6730d13, 2026-08-03. Two of the ten have closed since: C-16, when bb95e4b deleted HERB_TAG_FIRST, and C-15's enumeration half, when v3/CONSTANTS.md inventoried 305 constants (the values themselves stay underived, so C-15 is narrowed, not closed). The other eight were not re-checked against 8c8c787.

Where the two records disagree, and the seven that the precedence rule (first-hand chat > git blob > agent-written doc) settles. 1 The dates of the 07-01 quotes: chat wins — the conversation ran 06-27 → 07-01 and the doc dates the write-up, not the turns. 2 Who owns the v2 five-facet set: docs win — the 05-31 doc labels it [AGENT-ASSERTED] and the 06-25 doc has the user disowning it, "never hard-approved the specific five, and it hollowed the tag". 3 C-8's attribution: docs win — three verbatim 06-12 quotes make the node/attribute rule his own. 4 C-4's :NEXT claim: docs win — the 05-25 live audit shows :NEXT was never populated. 5 C-1's residue: docs win — the un-retracted "Status. Active" is his explicit frozen-v1-docs policy, "that shit is still true for THAT build". 6 C-17's cause: docs win — "this is ONLY RAGAS", said twice, a user decision. 7 C-6's novelty: docs win — the 06-27 content-profile recovery was argued two days earlier.

The eight items where the two records genuinely conflict or both fall silent, and this document does not pick a winner. 1 Graph magnitudes: the 05-14 pilot reports 5,843 chunks selected, 255,288 HAS_TAG edges and 25,896 unique tag names, while the 05-25 live audit reports Chunk 4,869, Tag 24,804, HAS_TAG 230,321 — eleven days apart, every figure lower, and which is right cannot be told from either record. 2 w_facet distinct values: 19 or 21, with the desktop record contradicting itself. 3 Whether max-then-sum was "never repudiated" — his 07-23 "it's NOT normalized AND it's summed? what fucking idiot combo is that!?" against, minutes later, "the difficult and relative part of them was how much they should matter/guide etc, not fucking if they are normalized and summed or not". 4 Which framing governs facets: 06-28 categorical or 06-27/07-01 dials — both records agree it is open, and an agent arbitrating its own precedence is not evidence. 5 The interpreter model sequence does not reconcile: no source states why the shipped arm's interpreter became Haiku. 6 Whether the pass-1 gold-100 output folders were deleted and by which commit. 7 How severe C-2 is. 8 Shared silences neither record can fill — why qt.scopeWeight was introduced, why the built tagger is z-ai/glm-5.1, prose authorship generally, how the corpus reached the machine, and what the DATA_README shipped by 7879dfe says about cross-arm metric validity.

Provenance of this document. It is a reorganisation of two existing forensic records into one chronology: no git object was read for it, no document was re-verified, no measurement was taken, and no conclusion appears that is not already in a source record. Sources, all read in full: git_record.md (1,760 lines), desktop_docs_record.md (1,575 lines), USER_CANON.md (1,577 lines at the b0fcadc snapshot; 1,589 at HEAD). Nothing under docs/canon/raw/ was modified and USER_CANON.md was not modified — both raw records remain on disk as evidence and remain the authority, and where this file and a raw record differ the raw record wins. Not opened: v3/data/questions.jsonl, gold100.jsonl, heldout100.jsonl, 10smoke.jsonl, per his 08-02 instruction, so every question-set figure quoted (1,514 = 815 + 699; the citation distribution min 11 / median 52 / mean 71 / p90 170 / p99 298 / max 683) is reproduced from inside a source record, not from the data.
